data.title: Japan Inflation Accelerates on Surging Cost of Daily Necessities — Market Talk
data.description: Higher oil prices amid Middle East tensions are increasingly feeding into Japan's consumer prices, particularly for daily necessities and durable goods, says NLI Research Institute economist Taro Saito. Inflation for daily essentials such as tissue paper, plastic bags and facial cleansers accelerated for a sixth straight month in October, rising 6.9% from a year earlier, from April's 1.5% gain, according to NLI estimates. "Higher crude oil prices are being passed on to retail prices with a time lag through rising costs for petrochemical products and packaging materials," Saito says. "Inflation for durable consumer goods is also steadily accelerating, driven by rising semiconductor and memory prices amid expanding global AI-related demand," he adds. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)

data.title: GME Stock Rises Overnight: Roaring Kitty’s Return After Nearly 2 Years Flips Retail Sentiment Bullish Amid GTA 6 Frenzy
data.description:
Key points:
  • Keith Gill, known as Roaring Kitty, returned to social media and posted a Cat Mario image. 
  • GameStop is also drawing attention following the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI and Trump’s share buy.
  • On Stocktwits, retail sentiment turned ‘bullish’ from ‘bearish’. 

GameStop Corp. (GME) stock edged higher overnight after Keith Gill, better known as Roaring Kitty, returned to X with his first post since January 2025. His mysterious Cat Mario image appeared alongside the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, sparking fresh interest among bullish retail traders who hoped for a repeat of the 2021 “meme stock” squeeze.

GameStop stock edged up 0.4% overnight Thursday after a 1.5% gain in regular session. The stock is also on track for a third week of gains.

Roaring Kitty Breaks Nearly Two-Year Social Media Silence

On Thursday, Gill dropped a single image of Cat Mario, the power-up from Nintendo’s Super Mario 3D World, on an account that had been silent for nearly two years. He added no caption or explanation.

Gill is the reason GameStop became the “meme stock”. His bullish commentary in 2020 and 2021 helped fuel a retail rally that squeezed hedge funds and turned him into a folk hero on Reddit. Since then, his posts have usually sent the stock higher.

GTA VI Launch, Trump Purchase Adds To GameStop Buzz

Roaring Kitty’s return to social media comes after the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, which is expected to bring more shoppers to GameStop stores to buy consoles and accessories. However, GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen is speaking out against the industry's growing shift toward digital game sales. He believes this change is bad for customers and could hurt GameStop's traditional business of selling physical video games.

Also, a U.S. government disclosure revealed that President Donald Trump bought between $1,001 and $15,000 worth of GameStop's stock.

What Are GME Retail Traders Saying

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock jumped to ‘bullish’ from ‘bearish’. The stock registered a 210% increase in message volume over the past week.

A user said, “Got silver and gold crashing while gme trending over kitty post !”

Another user said, “This is a totally different company to what it was 5/6 years ago. Cash in the bank. Invested in other ventures. Profitable, with really good margins. Management that is heavily invested. And it goes on and on.

Seems like RK is back on the scene , but even if he’s not, this investment is going to be fantastic. Can’t wait to see what develops in the future.”

A third user said, “Any chance this is a big nothing burger? Trying to stay optimistic but the chances of 2021 happening are slim to none.”

GME stock has gained 34% year-to-date.

data.title: How High Can ANT Stock Go? Wall Street Debut Sparks Valuation Debate – One Analyst Sees Amazon-Google Scale Opportunity In Anthropic
data.description:
Key points:
  • Needham put Anthropic in the same league as Amazon, Google and Microsoft.
  • Melius set the highest target at $155 over two years, nearly 60% above the debut close.
  • NYU Stern’s Aswath Damodaran valued Anthropic at about $76, citing higher data center costs and regulatory pressure.

Shares of Anthropic PBC (ANT) jumped 17% in their Wall Street debut on Thursday as analysts cast the Claude maker as a rare growth opportunity in the same league as Amazon and Google, with the most bullish target pointing to nearly 60% more upside.

ANT stock opened at $111.50 on Thursday before settling at $97.17, well above its $83 offer price even on a day the Nasdaq Composite fell over 2%.

The $81.34 billion offering overtook SpaceX’s June listing as the largest IPO on record. Alongside a separate $26 billion private placement, Anthropic expected to receive $104.8 billion after fees and expenses, giving it cash to fund the next generation of Claude.

Analyst Puts Anthropic In Big Tech’s League

Needham initiated coverage with a ‘Buy’ rating and a $150 target, implying 54% upside from current levels. “Growth opportunities like ANT rarely come along but we think history puts ANT in the same dominant bucket as fellow tech titans AMZN, GOOG, and MSFT,” the firm said.

Needham estimates that AI could address a tenth of the $56 trillion global labor market. Anthropic already earns more when customers put Claude to work on more tasks. Usage-based charges accounted for 79% of revenue in the first nine months of 2026, according to its prospectus.

Needham expects revenue to grow more than 150% in fiscal 2027 and believes Claude’s brand and Anthropic’s scale could drive operating margins above 35% over time, even as the company spends tens of billions of dollars a year training models.

William Blair also expects Anthropic to win a larger share of corporate budgets. “We think AI is a generational shift in the tech landscape, and Anthropic is leading the charge in developing AI with a select handful of other companies,” the firm said.

William Blair initiated coverage at ‘Outperform,’ calling the IPO valuation “very reasonable” at nine times estimated 2027 sales. It said a multiple of 17 to 20 times sales could put the stock at $130 to $150, or 34% to 54% above its debut close.

What It Would Take ANT To Hit $155

Melius initiated coverage at ‘Buy’ with a two-year target of $155, implying nearly 60% upside from Anthropic’s $97.17 debut close. The firm expects customers to use Claude more often and buy more products as the cost per task falls. Over time, it sees earnings power above $5 a share and operating margins above 30%.

Melius also pointed to Anthropic’s flexibility. Claude can run on chips from Nvidia and AMD, as well as Amazon’s Trainium and Google’s TPUs. “If the model scales accordingly, shares could trade at a nice premium to hyperscalers given its outsized growth and high gross margins,” the firm said.

Additionally, Wolfe Research initiated coverage at ‘Outperform’ with a $135 target, implying 39% upside from the same close.

Cathie Wood Sees Edge In Unreleased Models

Citizens pointed to Claude’s role in building its own successor as a reason for its ‘Market Outperform’ rating. “Over 90% of the contributions to our codebase in September 2026 were written by Claude,” Anthropic said in its prospectus. Citizens’ $125 target implies 28.6% upside from the debut close.

Meanwhile, ARK Investment Management CEO Cathie Wood sees an edge in the models Anthropic keeps in-house. She estimates AI training costs are falling about 75% a year, allowing Anthropic to train better models while giving rivals fewer chances to learn from its most advanced work. Wood compared the potential lead over open-weight models to a decade of progress at the slower pace of earlier chip advances. “It would be like being 10 years ahead in that world,” she said.

ANT Valuations Below Debut Close

Morningstar kept its fair value estimate at $92, about 5% below Thursday’s close, with a ‘3-star’ rating. It sees Claude’s meeting and spreadsheet tools as an early test of whether businesses will shift spending from existing software to Anthropic as Claude takes on more valuable work. With about $900 billion in computing commitments, Morningstar believes Anthropic’s cash and IPO proceeds can cover its near-term bills even if sales stop growing. A drop in sales would be tougher. “I think declines in revenue would be quite difficult for the company to manage,” Morningstar said.

Similarly, NYU Stern professor Aswath Damodaran valued Anthropic at about $76 a share after accounting for employee options, which is 22% below its debut close. His estimate assumes higher data center construction costs and tighter regulation will weigh on profits.

How Do Retail Traders Feel About ANT?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ANT was ‘extremely bullish’ amid a 885% surge in 24-hour message volumes.

One user said they would buy at $65. Another user said they would wait for $75. A separate user said they were sticking with Nvidia, Intel and SpaceX, adding, “Long-term holding has always been my strategy, and I’m not changing it now.”

View this Stocktwits post

Most voters in a Stocktwits poll sat out Anthropic’s debut, with 68% of the 17,500 votes going to “Avoiding it.” Another 16% chose to buy for the long term, 9% favored a short-term trade and 7% planned to trade around the volatility.

data.title: Japan futures set for worst week since June on tepid Tokyo equities, tyre demand
data.description:
By Emily Ou Yong

Japanese rubber futures slipped for a fourth consecutive session on Friday and were set for their biggest weekly loss since late June, pressured by a selloff in Asian equities and soft tyre demand.

  • The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for April delivery , was down 1.2 yen, or 0.28%, at 421.6 yen ($2.64) per kg, as of 0200 GMT

  • The contract has lost 4.55% so far this week

  • The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery fell 130 yuan, or 0.69%, to 18,595 yuan ($2,789.32) per metric ton

  • The most active January butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) rose 260 yuan, or 1.7%, to 15,525 yuan per metric ton

  • Recent weak macroeconomic sentiment coupled with sluggish downstream demand has led to a renewed bearish market sentiment, analysts from Gelin Dahua Futures said in a note

  • Japan's Nikkei tumbled 4.1% and was headed for a 6.8% weekly drop, as Asian shares slid to be on track for their worst week since 2020 after Anthropic's debut failed to restore investor faith in AI trades, while the dollar extended a rally on safe-haven flows

  • Capacity utilisation at sampled Chinese semi-steel and all-steel tyre makers was 62.05% and 58.72% in the week ended November 19, down 7.31 and 3.32 percentage points respectively from a year earlier, data from commodity information provider Longzhong Information showed

  • Raw materials entered a high production phase in top producer Thailand, with rubber tapping operations improving in the northeast region, said analysts from GF Futures in a note

  • The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for February delivery (STFG7) last traded at 238.4 U.S. cents per kg, down 0.7%

($1 = 159.6700 yen)

data.title: Anthropic’s blockbuster float signals AI cash - but not a funding boom for all
data.description:
Anthropic’s record float shows there is money for AI, but its retreat from the opening trade suggests Australian software companies should not count on investors funding every AI ambition on generous terms.

A record with a retreat

Anthropic briefly reached a valuation of A$3tn when its shares began trading, before retreating off earlier session highs. The developer of Claude nevertheless closed its first session 17% above the offer price, with a US$1.27tn market capitalisation.

That is a powerful result for Anthropic as it raises capital to pursue AI growth, despite facing significant uncertainty as a result of it's very large future committed funding requirements and slowing revenue growth.

Revenue meets computing costs

Anthropic has the scale to explain the demand. Its filing records US$33.2bn of revenue in the nine months to September 2026, alongside a heavy operating loss. The company also cautions that its recent revenue growth may not continue at comparable rates.

The spending commitments are just as important as the sales. Anthropic has committed to spending substantial sums under its Microsoft contract, regardless of actual usage. Its separate, conditional private placement is backed by Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC Partners. Those proposed investments sit alongside the public offer, rather than forming part of its proceeds.

We think the lesson is selective capital, not a universal AI premium. Investors have backed a business with substantial revenue, but that revenue comes with formidable future costs.

The market has priced in a very heavy premium on Anthropic, and with OpenAI potentially hitting the boards early next year, there is a question of where continued funding will come from.

Capital could spread

The strongest counterargument is that a record float can draw more money into technology broadly. Investors who miss out on Anthropic shares, including Australian applicants whose allocations are determined by their brokers, may look elsewhere for exposure. That could improve funding conditions for smaller software businesses as well as large AI developers. The recent fall in the price of Bitcoin may indicate a general rotation out of crypto into the AI trade.

However, past history suggests that there will be cheaper entry points available into Anthropic. The previous record holder was SpaceX, whose share later traded below their offer price not long after floating. Abundant initial demand and selective subsequent investing can coexist; especially where early VC investors need to provide returns for their investors.

Domestically, all eyes will continue on Firmus and domestic data centre operators like NextDC that have not shared the same recent enthusiasm of US markets. Firmus spectacularly pulled it's IPO back in October after trying to re-cut the book to save the deal, and NextDC has seen it's share price collapse from just under $15 in mid August to just above $5 a share in October. It has subsequently bounced back to around $10.

data.title: US Army postpones detonations of degraded lead compound in Iowa
data.description:
Key points:
  • Explosions at Iowa Army Ammunition Plant delayed until Monday
  • Environmental groups ask appeals court to halt EPA permit for lead azide detonations
  • EPA permit requires public notifications, blast-containment measures and corrective action

By Daniel Trotta

The US Army on Thursday said it had postponed controlled explosions of a stockpile of a degraded lead compound in Iowa that had been scheduled for Friday after nearby residents protested and environmental groups filed a lawsuit.

Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle announced on X the detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown would be postponed until Monday, which he described as the latest possible moment before a forecast temperature drop that he said would "risk further destabilization of the material."

The office of Iowa US Senator Chuck Grassley had said the Army was concerned a spontaneous explosion of the lead azide, a compound used in detonators, would be "catastrophic" and saw two controlled blasts as the safest way to dispose of the stockpile.

In an emergency motion filed on Thursday, the Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club asked the 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals to halt an EPA permit allowing the destruction of 68 drums of the compound. The groups argued the disposal method would disperse toxic lead dust over a broad area of Iowa and potentially Illinois and that the EPA failed to require sufficient safeguards or adequately evaluate alternatives while denying the public a meaningful opportunity to comment.

The EPA did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

The EPA permit imposed numerous conditions, including public notifications, blast-containment measures, and corrective action for any contamination resulting from the blasts.

Local opponents, some of whom had been advised to leave their homes during the operation, had complained that people were given insufficient warning and said the Army and local and federal officials had not responded to their concerns.

"Public communication is essential to public trust. Therefore, the Army will continue to actively engage with state and local officials throughout the region to distribute accurate, up-to-date information," Telle said in announcing the delay.

Telle said the Army uncovered the degraded lead azide in March and began informing local officials about the danger it posed. Some people in the area said they only recently became aware. A small group staged a protest on the highway near the facility on Wednesday, and some local politicians urged a postponement.

Jill Holler, who organized Wednesday's protest, said she was disappointed the delay was only for three days.

data.title: Uncertainty Over Indonesia's Mining Policy Raises Cost Concerns — Market Talk
data.description: Uncertainty over Indonesia's mining policy raises concerns about operating costs amid financial strain for miners, CreditSights analysts Jonathan Tan Jun Jie and Lakshmanan R say in a note. President Prabowo Subianto has proposed that at least 70% of proceeds generated under mining permits accrue to the state and suggested the government could take controlling stakes in mining companies, they note. How the 70% share would be calculated and implemented remains unclear, making the potential impact difficult to assess, they say. Meanwhile, Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia plans to impose a single-digit dollar-per-ton service fee on palm oil exports, with fees on coal and ferroalloys still undecided. These developments warrant a continued risk premium for the mining sector, they add. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)

data.title: Why Is INTU Stock Falling Overnight?
data.description:
Key points:
  • Intuit reported Q1 results above expectations and raised its full year sales view.
  • Intuit is selling Mailchimp for $3.68 billion to Bending Spoons.
  • Retail sentiment for INTU shifted to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish.’

Intuit, Inc. (INTU) shares plunged on Thursday despite the tax filing software firm’s strong quarterly report and a major divestiture, underscoring continued anxiety over the future of Saas companies in the AI era.

INTU fell 8.3% in overnight trading. Shares have already lost over 52% in 2026. However, retail sentiment for the stock on Stocktwits climbed higher, with traders calling to buy the dip.

Mailchimp Sale

Among the key items in the earnings, Intuit said it was selling Mailchimp for $3.68 billion to Bending Spoons (BSP), the owner of several wayward tech brands. The purchase price includes $3.31 billion in cash and $368 million in Bending Spoons stock. BSP rose 4.8% in after-hours trading.

Bending Spoons, which went public in July, owns AOL, Everbrite, Evernote, Vimeo and others. The deal comes about a month after Berkshire Hathaway invested $930 million in Bending Spoons, accumulating a 4% stake.

"We have built AI native experiences to help businesses win new customers, manage their pipeline and help them grow through our lead-to-cash capabilities,” Intuit CEO Sasan Goodarzi said on the analyst call.

“Selling Mailchimp sharpens our focus behind that strategy while positioning Mailchimp and its team for continued success in their next chapter with Bending Spoons."

Intuit is known for its tax software such as QuickBooks, TurboTax, Credit Karma.

Intuit’s Quarterly Update

Intuit reported a higher profit as revenue rose 12% to $4.35 billion in its fiscal first quarter, with results topping analyst estimates. Sales in Intuit’s business-facing segment increased 15%, while its consumer-facing sales rose 7%.

Intuit’s second quarter forecasts – revenue of $4.93 billion to $4.95 billion, with earnings per share between $2.55 and $2.60 – were below expectations, but the company raised its full year sales view.

The company now expects revenue between $23.08 billion to $23.37 billion, down from its prior view for $23.28 billion to $23.51 billion.

In Q1, we saw higher interest rates weigh on growth as well as impact from a shift in consumer behavior. Our Q2 guidance assumes the demand environment remains at current levels,” CFO Sandeep Aujla said on the analyst call.

"Based on the Credit Karma performance and trends we have discussed, we are updating our full year revenue outlook. This update is limited to Credit Karma with corresponding adjustments to Consumer segment and total company revenue guidance."

Retail View On INTU

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for INTU shifted to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish,’ with the ticker trending on the platform.

“Still very bullish after today’s earnings report,” a trader wrote.

“Selling Mailchimp is a good thing for the long term. And taxes have to be done by everyone. This will be back over 400 a share sometime in the next 12 months. Today’s dip under 270 was a huge buying opportunity and I’m glad to be a holder of Intuit.”

Another wrote: “$INTU shorts are desperate. Back over 300 soon.” As of the last close, INTU had declined 52.5% year to date.

data.title: SoftBank shares slump 15% as AI worries drown Asian chipmaker stocks
data.description:
Shares of SoftBank Group Corp., Japan's investment holding behemoth, slumped by as much as 16% intraday on Friday as Japan’s major stock indexes slid as concerns about the artificial intelligence trade dampened investor sentiment.

The chip-heavy Nikkei 225 Stock Average fell by as much as 4.6%, while the broader Topix dropped up to 2.8%.

Apart from SoftBank Group Corp., chipmakers led the decline in Friday morning trading. Kioxia Holdings Corp. and Ibiden Co. each falling more than 10%.

This follows a massive crash on Wall Street, despite a mammoth Anthropic debut crippled under AI pressure. The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 2.25% or over 550 points in the session Thursday.

SOFTBANK's AI EXPOSURE

In its November 10 earnings report for the quarter, the Japanese investment powerhouse with substantial exposure to AI reported a second-quarter net loss of $7 billion. The result was weighed down by significant data-centre construction costs in the US and rising financing payments.

The impact this quarter from a subsidiary’s advance payments for power-generation equipment may be partly balanced by rebates on future purchases. SoftBank’s borrowing could pose a greater concern, as financing costs more than doubled between July and September.

The group raised $56.5 billion during the period, its largest quarterly total on record, as founder Masayoshi Son pressed ahead with aggressive AI investment. The spending has covered data centres and robotics, as well as the $64.6 billion acquisition of a 13% stake in ChatGPT developer OpenAI.

data.title: Massachusetts' top court to hear Lindsay Clancy's bid to toss murder charges
data.description:
Key points:
  • State high court to hear case in January ahead of March 29 retrial
  • Clancy faces first-degree murder charges over 2023 deaths of three children
  • Prosecutors urge high court to reject appeal without hearing

By Nate Raymond

Massachusetts' highest court said on Thursday it will hear arguments in Lindsay Clancy's bid to dismiss the murder charges stemming from the 2023 deaths of her three young children and avoid being tried a second time.

Justice Elizabeth Dewar said review by the full Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court was warranted and the case would be heard in January, ahead of Clancy's planned March 29 retrial.

Judge William Sullivan in Plymouth had scheduled the retrial during a hearing on Monday, a week after he rejected arguments that a second trial would run afoul of Clancy's protection under the US Constitution's Fifth Amendment against being tried twice for the same crime, known as double jeopardy.

Sullivan on September 4 declared a mistrial after the jury in her initial trial reported that a holdout juror was preventing it from reaching a unanimous verdict. Clancy's lawyers in their appeal contend that the mistrial declaration had not been manifestly necessary.

"We are pleased that the state supreme judicial court will receive briefs and hear oral argument on an issue of great importance – whether Ms Clancy’s constitutionally guaranteed double jeopardy rights prohibit a second prosecution," defense attorney Martin Weinberg said in a statement.

Clancy, 36, faces first-degree murder charges over the deaths of her daughter Cora, 5; son Dawson, 3; and 8-month-old son Callan. If convicted of those charges, she would be sentenced to life in prison without parole.

No one at Clancy's initial trial disputed that she strangled the children with exercise bands on January 24, 2023, in the basement of their home in the Boston suburb of Duxbury. She then cut herself with a knife and jumped from a second-story window in an attempt to end ​her own life, leaving her paralyzed.

Clancy's lawyers have argued the evidence showed she was in the throes of postpartum psychosis when she killed her children and should be found not guilty by reason of insanity, known in Massachusetts as lack of criminal responsibility.

Citing jury notes that stated the holdout juror was not following the law on reasonable doubt despite the judge's instructions, defense lawyers in Clancy's appeal said that rather than declare a mistrial, Sullivan should have instead questioned the holdout and potentially removed the juror.

Plymouth County District Attorney Timothy Cruz's office in a brief on Wednesday countered that the high court should reject Clancy's appeal without a hearing so prosecutors could "continue to pursue justice for Cora, Dawson, and Callan Clancy."

data.title: Fairfax arm gets controlling 44% stake in IIFL Capital
data.description:
FIH Mauritius Investments, an arm of Fairfax Financial Holdings, has acquired a controlling stake of 44.08 per cent in IIFL Capital Services Ltd.

FIH Mauritius Investments and HWIC Asia Fund, a person acting in concert (PAC), following the completion of an open offer and share purchases, have raised their stakes in IIFL Capital.

Kalki Family Private Trust (acting through its trustee) and Ardent Impex Private Ltd are collectively referred to as the 'new sellers' and have agreed to sell 30 lakh shares of IIFL Capital to FIH Mauritius Investments, IIFL Capital said in a regulatory filing.

The new sellers decided to sell shares on November 18, it said.

Consequent to the investment agreement, FIH Mauritius Investments launched an open offer in terms of regulatory requirements. On November 18, 2026, the Open Offer concluded, it said.

An open offer allows an investor acquiring a significant stake in a listed company to offer to buy shares from its existing public shareholders.

With effect from November 19, the acquirer has become a promoter of the target company.

Separately, FIH Mauritius Investments Ltd bought 4.40 crore shares, representing a 13.95 per cent stake in IIFL Capital Services, according to block deal data on the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The shares were purchased at an average price of ₹350 apiece, taking the deal value to ₹1,540 crore.

FIH Mauritius Investments' direct holding consequently rose to 40.79 per cent from 26.84 per cent, while Fairfax's combined stake through its affiliates stood at 44.08 per cent, as per the exchange data.

The transaction also marked a dilution of the existing promoter group's holding, which offloaded an equal number of shares at the same price.

IIFL Group founder Nirmal Bhanwarlal Jain sold 3.23 crore shares, or a 10.24 per cent stake, for ₹1,130.50 crore, and Venkataraman Rajamani offloaded 87 lakh shares for ₹304.50 crore.

Promoter group entities, Ardent Impex and Kalki Family Private Trust, also sold shares worth ₹70 crore and ₹35 crore, respectively.

The combined holding of promoters and promoter group entities fell to 11.85 per cent from 25.80 per cent after the transactions.

The latest transaction comes a day after Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa's Fairfax group sold over 5.65 crore shares, representing a 13.24 per cent stake, in IIFL Finance for ₹3,488 crore through 39 tranches.

The divestment from IIFL Finance comes amid Fairfax's proposed acquisition of nearly 61 per cent in IDBI Bank for around ₹53,000 crore announced in October.

The proposed IDBI Bank acquisition had fuelled expectations that Fairfax would pare some of its Indian investments to part-finance the transaction.

Fairfax also holds stakes in Go Digit's insurance business.

Shares of IIFL Capital Services declined 5.35 per cent to close at ₹334.20 apiece on the NSE.

data.title: Ashoka Buildcon shares in focus after Saudi Arabia firms cancels ₹850 crore project due to 'internal reasons'
data.description:
Shares of Ashoka Buildcon Ltd. are in focus on Friday, November 20, after the company its Diriyah project worth nearly ₹850 crore has been cancelled.

The company, on Thursday, updated the exchanges regarding the letter of acceptance that its Saudi Arabian subsidiary 'Ashoka Buildcon Ltd. for Contracting', in a joint venture with BEC Arabia Contracting Co, was awarded by Saudi Arabia's Diriyah Company.

The joint venture formed for the main construction works of Diriyah II - delivery partner for One Hotel. Of the JV, Ashoka Buildcon's share was of ₹846.38 crore.

The company said the Diriyah Company notified the joint venture that the project was been cancelled due to "internal reasons". It said it was in the process of approaching the employer to understand the reason in better detail and the next course of action.

The company had informed the exchanges of the order in February 2026 and had started the initial work on the same. Ashoka Buildcon had booked a revenue of around ₹24.4 crore. The company is confident of recovering the amount from the client.

As of the September quarter, Ashoka Buildcon's order backlog stood at 16,000 crore, 2.7 times the total trailing months (TTM) revenues. Post the cancellation, the order backlog will stand at ₹15,100 crore, 2.6 times the TTM revenues.

Shares of Ashoak Buildcon ended the previous session 2% lower at ₹112.9 apiece. The stock has gained 10.5% in the past month, but is down 10.7% in the last six months and has declined 32.8% this year, so far.

data.title: Magna Mining Announces Filing of the NI 43-101 Preliminary Economic Assessment Technical Report for the Levack Mine in Sudbury, Ontario
data.description:
SUDBURY, Ontario, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Magna Mining Inc. TSXV:NICU OTCQX:MGMNF FSE:8YD (“Magna” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce that further to its news release dated October 8, 2026 titled “Magna Mining Reports Results of Levack Mine Preliminary Economic Assessment and Approves Restart of Production” the Company has filed on SEDAR+ an independent technical report titled “Levack Mine Preliminary Economic Assessment”.

The technical report was prepared in accordance with National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects. data.title: Seoul appeals court upholds acquittal of Kakao founder on stock manipulation charges
data.description:
A South Korean appeals court on Friday upheld the acquittal of Kim Beom-su, founder of tech firm Kakao Corp , on charges of manipulating the share price of K-pop agency SM Entertainment , rejecting prosecutors' bid to overturn the lower court ruling, according to Yonhap news agency.

  • The Seoul High Court said the evidence submitted by prosecutors did not prove that Kim intended to manipulate prices artificially or had conspired to do so.

  • Prosecutors had asked the court in September to jail Kim for 15 years and fine him 500 million won ($375,000), seeking to reverse the October 2025 ruling by the Seoul Southern District Court that cleared him of all charges.

  • Kim, also known as Brian Kim, was arrested in July 2024 on charges of helping to manipulate the stock price of SM Entertainment in 2023 to prevent rival Hybe from acquiring the K-pop agency. He was released on bail in October 2024.

  • Kim has denied the allegations, saying he never ordered or tolerated any illegal activity.

  • In a statement, Kim thanked the court for its "wise decision" and called the verdict "an important turning point" in dispelling three years of uncertainty around Kakao.

  • Kakao shares were up 0.31% shortly after the verdict, while the wider market fell 4.2% .

($1 = 1,332.7700 won)

data.title: Adani Energy Solutions wins power transmission deal in India's Bihar
data.description:
Adani Energy Solutions has won a transmission contract in the eastern Indian state of Bihar that carries an annual tariff of INR5bn (about $54mn), Press Trust of India reported on November 19. The network will carry 2,400 MW of electricity from a thermal power station that sister company Adani Power is building at Pirpainti.

The award connects a new Adani generating asset to the grid through infrastructure built by another arm of the same group, extending the conglomerate's reach across the power value chain. India is adding both generating capacity and grid links to keep pace with rising electricity consumption, and both demand heavy investment.

A statement from the company said it won the contract through the tariff-based competitive bidding (TBCB) process. The project involves building 881 circuit kilometres of transmission lines and adding 3,160 MVA of capacity for transformation, with completion targeted for the fourth quarter of 2028.

A special purpose vehicle called Vikramshila Power Transmission Ltd will carry out the scheme, formally titled the Evacuation of Power from 3X800 MW STPP Pirpainti project. The Pirpainti plant will use ultra-supercritical technology.

Jhanjharpur, Bethauli and Begusarai will host four substations of the gas-insulated type, planned alongside the associated transmission lines and transformation equipment. According to the company, the network will also strengthen Bihar's broader transmission grid and improve the reliability of the state's electricity supply.

Kandarp Patel, chief executive officer of Adani Energy Solutions, said the scheme would give the 2,400 MW of new generation a strong evacuation route while bolstering the backbone of Bihar's grid.

When the project is finished, the company expects its network to cover 30,683 circuit kilometres, with transformation capacity rising to 146,585 MVA. The value of transmission work in its capital expenditure pipeline will grow to about INR915bn.

According to the company, it serves around 13mn consumers across Mumbai and the Mundra special economic zone. Adani Energy Solutions has operations spanning smart metering, the distribution of electricity and the transmission of power.

data.title: Chicago soybeans set for weekly drop as dollar firms, wheat, corn decline
data.description:
Chicago soybeans declined for a fifth straight session on Friday and are set to book a weekly drop, weighed down by a stronger dollar that makes US soybeans less competitive.

Wheat futures declined, but are poised to log a second weekly gain, while corn fell on Friday and is likely to post a weekly loss.

FUNDAMENTALS

  • The most-traded soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) was down 0.08% at $12.06-1/2 a bushel at 0123 GMT

  • Chicago wheat fell 0.21% at $5.93-3/4 a bushel and CBOT corn was down 0.28% at $ 4.37-3/4 a bushel

  • The US Department of Agriculture reported net export sales of US soybeans in the week ended November 12 at 1,501,000 metric tons for the current marketing year, within a range of trade expectations for 1 million to 2 million tons, and private sales of 200,844 metric tons of soybeans to Mexico for 2026/27 delivery

  • The United States generated 1.26 billion ethanol blending (D6) credits in October, up from 1.19 billion in September, while biodiesel blending credits (D4) fell to 758 million, from 792 million in September, according to Environmental Protection Agency data

  • A group of South Korean flour mills has issued an international tender to purchase around 100,000 metric tons of milling wheat to be sourced from the United States only, while the Taiwan Flour Millers' Association has issued an international tender to purchase an estimated 89,000 metric tons of grade 1 milling wheat to be sourced from the United States, European traders said

  • Jordan's state grain buyer has issued an international tender to buy up to 120,000 metric tons of milling wheat which can be sourced from optional origins, European traders said on Thursday

  • Argentina's 2026/27 wheat harvest is progressing with yields above expectations, the Buenos Aires grains exchange said, estimating the crop at 23.4 million tons, the second-highest production of the grain in the country

  • Grain exports through Romania's Black Sea port of Constanta rose by double digits in the first 10 months of the year, the port authority said, helped by a good harvest, strong demand and Ukrainian exports passing through the port.

  • The International Grains Council has lowered its forecast for 2026/27 global corn production at 1.301 billion metric tons, down 6 million from last month's forecast, driven largely by downgrades for the US and Ukraine, and raised its 2026/27 world wheat crop outlook by 6 million tons to 826 million, reflecting upgrades in Argentina, Turkey, Egypt and Australia

  • Russia's annual capacity to ship grain from its ports on the Baltic Sea and in the Arctic has quadrupled since July following Ukrainian drone attacks in the Black Sea region, a senior executive at the country's railway monopoly said on Thursday.MARKET NEWS

  • Global stocks fell on Thursday, with tech shares sliding as Anthropic's ANT.O debut failed to allay investor concerns about AI returns, while oil prices rose as attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz grabbed market attention.

  • The dollar held near a 19-month high on Friday, after rising over the past eight sessions as jitters over the AI trade sent investors to safe-haven assets, while the yen steadied after Japanese inflation data.
